description: The god of lightning and the god of trickery: adventure duo, then enemies at Ragnarök. Two faces of the Scandinavian pantheon.

hero.hook: One hits with a hammer. The other lies to win. Together, they save Asgard… until the day Loki betrays her.

blocks.text: **Thor** and **Loki** are the two most popular figures in Norse mythology. Thor protects men with lightning. Loki sows disorder with trickery. We often come across them together in travel stories.

Their bond is not a simple comic friendship. It shows the tension between the order of the gods and chaos. From prankish companionship to the final war, here's how this alliance is built... then broken.

These myths come from Scandinavian peoples from the 5th to the 12th centuries. We know them mainly thanks to late Icelandic texts, written when the region was already Christianized. The major source is , written around **1220** by **Snorri Sturluson**, supplemented by . [[Edda in prose]] [[Poetic Edda]]

blocks.caption: Asgard and Midgard connected by the Bifröst, the rainbow bridge.

blocks.text: The world is organized around , the cosmic tree. Top: **Asgard**, home of the gods. Lower: **Midgard**, world of men, connected by the **Bifröst**. The gods are divided into two clans: the **Aesir**, led by **Odin** (war and sovereignty), and the **Vanes**, like Freyr and Freyja (fertility). [[Yggdrasil]]
In ancient texts, the Bifröst is a fragile bridge: at Ragnarök, it will tremble and collapse under the weight of the giants.

**Thor** is the son of Odin and Earth. He is the most revered god of the people: he defends humanity against the **giants**, unleashed forces of nature. Bearded and red hair, he embodies a clear and straight strength.

blocks.caption: Mjöllnir, Thor's hammer: it strikes and returns to the hand.

blocks.text: His weapon, **Mjöllnir**, forged by dwarves, shatters mountains and always returns to his hand. A belt of strength and iron gloves help him wield it. His name gave the **Thursday** (Thor's day) in Germanic languages. Unlike the more aristocratic Odin, Thor is the god of free peasants: rain, harvest, safe home.
Thor's chariot is pulled by two goats. If he's hungry, he can eat them in the evening and resurrect them the next day with his hammer... as long as he doesn't break any bones.

**Loki** lives among the Aesir, but he is of giant blood. He joined the pantheon through a blood pact with Odin. He's the **trickster**: his pranks and lies are disturbing, but they also move the story forward and sometimes offer the gods their greatest treasures.

blocks.caption: Loki, god of trickery: useful ally, announced traitor.

blocks.text: It changes shape and even sex. In mare form, he becomes the mother of , Odin's eight-legged horse. With the giantess Angrboda, he generates three monsters: the wolf **Fenrir**, the snake **Jörmungandr** and **Hel**, guardian of the dead. Little by little, the prank becomes treason: he organizes the death of the luminous god **Baldr**. From then on, his fate was sealed. [[Sleipnir]]

sections.title: Loki, the ruse that ends badly

blocks.text: For a long time, Thor and Loki complemented each other. When the giant Thrym steals Mjöllnir, Thor disguises himself as a bride and Loki as a servant to retrieve it. Where the hammer fails, the lie succeeds, and vice versa.

Then the alliance breaks up. In **Ragnarök**, the twilight of the gods, Loki leads the enemies of Asgard. Thor confronts Jörmungandr, son of Loki: he kills the serpent, then dies of its venom after nine steps. Strength and cunning are annihilated together.

**Thor** and **Loki** embody the tension between protective force and disruptive cunning. Their bond, from comic friendship to the hatred of Ragnarök, shows how fragile the order of the gods remains in the face of chaos.
